records.source: וַיֹּ֨סֶף ע֥וֹד דָּוִ֛ד אֶת־כָּל־בָּח֥וּר בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל שְׁלֹשִׁ֥ים אָֽלֶף׃
records.gloss: And gathered again David every chosen [man] in Israel, thirty thousand.
pieces: David again gathered all the chosen men of Israel, thirty thousand.

L.1: And David again gathered every chosen [man] in Israel, thirty thousand.

R.1: Once more David called together the best fighting men in Israel, thirty thousand of them.

decisions.choice: gathered again: called together once more
decisions.reason: The verb means "gather, assemble". With "again" it looks back to the times David had already brought Israel together: when the tribes came to make him king (5:1-3) and when he led them against the Philistines (5:17-25). Now he gathers them for a new purpose, to bring the ark to his city.

decisions.choice: every chosen man in Israel: picked men in their prime
decisions.reason: The word means "chosen" and is used of young men at their strongest and of picked troops (1 Samuel 24:3; 26:2). The escort for the ark is gathered like an army, as the ark had once gone out with Israel's army (1 Samuel 4:3-4).

decisions.choice: thirty thousand: the number as written
decisions.reason: The word for "thousand" can also name a unit of troops, which would make the company smaller; see the note at Numbers 1. Here it is given as a number.

decisions.choice: the best fighting men
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly who the "chosen" men were: the picked men of Israel's fighting force.

records.heading: The ark is brought to Jerusalem

records.source: וַיָּ֣קָם׀וַיֵּ֣לֶךְ דָּוִ֗ד וְכָל־הָעָם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר אִתּ֔וֹ מִֽבַּעֲלֵ֖י יְהוּדָ֑ה לְהַעֲל֣וֹת מִשָּׁ֗ם אֵ֚ת אֲר֣וֹן הָאֱלֹהִ֔ים אֲשֶׁר־נִקְרָ֣א שֵׁ֗ם שֵׁ֣ם יְהוָ֧ה צְבָא֛וֹת יֹשֵׁ֥ב הַכְּרֻבִ֖ים עָלָֽיו׃
records.gloss: And arose and went David and all the people who [were] with him from Baale-judah to bring up from there [the] ark of the God, which is called [the] name, [the] name of Yahweh of hosts, sitting [on] the cherubim over it.
pieces: Then David and all the people with him set out from Baale-judah to bring the ark of God up from there, the ark which is called by the name, the name of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies, who sits enthroned on the cherubim above it.

L.2: And David arose and went, and all the people who [were] with him, from Baale-judah, to bring up from there the ark of God, which is called by the name, the name of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts, who sits [on] the cherubim over it.

R.2: Then David and all the people with him went from Baale-judah to bring the ark of God up from there. The ark bears the name of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies. He sits as king above the cherubim, the winged creatures on the lid of the ark.

decisions.choice: Baale-judah: another name for Kiriath-jearim
decisions.reason: Baale-judah means "the Baalahs of Judah"; the name may also be read as "Baalah of Judah". Joshua 15:9 says "Baalah, that is, Kiriath-jearim", and 1 Chronicles 13:6 tells this story with both names. The ark had stayed there in the house of Abinadab ever since the Philistines sent it back (1 Samuel 7:1-2).

decisions.choice: from Baale-judah: as the Hebrew text reads
alternatives: went to Baale-judah, to bring up from there the ark (as 1 Chronicles 13:6)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says David went "from" Baale-judah "to bring up from there" the ark. Read as it stands, the story begins as the company leaves the town with the ark. The same story in 1 Chronicles 13:6 says David went up "to" Baalah, and a slip of one letter in copying could explain the difference here. The place is the same either way; only the starting point of the journey differs.

decisions.choice: which is called by the name, the name of the LORD: the ark bears the LORD's own name
alternatives: which is called by the name of the LORD of hosts (the word once)
where the name of the LORD of hosts is called on
decisions.reason: To have someone's name called over a thing means that it belongs to him (Deuteronomy 28:10; Jeremiah 7:10-11; 1 Kings 8:43). The Hebrew writes the word "name" twice. This may be for emphasis, "the name, the very name", or a copyist may have written the word twice; 1 Chronicles 13:6 and the Greek have it once. The meaning is the same either way.

decisions.choice: the LORD of hosts who sits enthroned on the cherubim: the same title as at the ark's loss
decisions.reason: This is the title given to the ark when it was carried out of Shiloh into the battle where it was captured (1 Samuel 4:4). Now, as the ark is brought up to David's city, the writer gives the full title again. The differences: in 1 Samuel 4:4 it is "the ark of the covenant of the LORD of hosts", while here it is "the ark of God" that is called by the LORD's name; and here the cherubim are "over it", on the ark's cover (Exodus 25:18-22).

decisions.choice: sits: sits enthroned, reigns
decisions.reason: As in 1 Samuel 4:4, the verb "sit" said of a king means to sit on a throne. The LORD is pictured as king seated above the cherubim, with the ark as his footstool (1 Chronicles 28:2; Psalm 99:1).

decisions.choice: all the people who were with him: the chosen men of verse 1
decisions.reason: "The people" here are the men David had gathered (verse 1), though by verse 5 all Israel has joined the celebration.

decisions.choice: the LORD of Armies
decisions.reason: As everywhere in these books, Balanced and Readable say "Armies" for "hosts", the plainer word for what the title means; Literal keeps "hosts".

decisions.choice: The ark bears the name of ...; He sits as king above the cherubim, the winged creatures on the lid of the ark
decisions.reason: Readable says once that the ark bears the LORD's name rather than repeating "name", and explains the cherubim in the words used at 1 Samuel 4:4, in a new sentence.

records.source: וַיַּרְכִּ֜בוּ אֶת־אֲר֤וֹן הָֽאֱלֹהִים֙ אֶל־עֲגָלָ֣ה חֲדָשָׁ֔ה וַיִּשָּׂאֻ֔הוּ מִבֵּ֥ית אֲבִינָדָ֖ב אֲשֶׁ֣ר בַּגִּבְעָ֑ה וְעֻזָּ֣א וְאַחְי֗וֹ בְּנֵי֙ אֲבִ֣ינָדָ֔ב נֹהֲגִ֖ים אֶת־הָעֲגָלָ֥ה חֲדָשָֽׁה׃
records.gloss: And they made ride [the] ark of the God on [a] cart new, and they carried it from [the] house of Abinadab which [was] on the hill; and Uzzah and Ahio, [the] sons of Abinadab, [were] driving the cart new.
pieces: They placed the ark of God on a new cart and took it away from Abinadab's house on the hill, while Uzzah and Ahio, the sons of Abinadab, drove the new cart.

L.3: And they set the ark of God on a new cart and carried it from the house of Abinadab, which [was] on the hill; and Uzzah and Ahio, the sons of Abinadab, [were] driving the new cart.

R.3: They put the ark of God on a new cart and took it from Abinadab's house on the hill. Abinadab's sons Uzzah and Ahio were guiding the cart.

decisions.choice: set on a new cart: carried by oxen instead of on men's shoulders
decisions.reason: A new cart, never used for ordinary work, was a mark of respect. But it was how the Philistines had sent the ark back (1 Samuel 6:7-8). The law gave the holy things to the Levites of Kohath to carry on their shoulders with poles (Exodus 25:14; Numbers 4:15; 7:9). When David tried again, the ark was carried (verse 13), and 1 Chronicles 15:13-15 says the first attempt failed because this was not done.

decisions.choice: on the hill: a hill at Kiriath-jearim
decisions.reason: As in 1 Samuel 7:1, which uses the same words. The word can also be the name of the town Gibeah, but here it points to the high ground where Abinadab's house stood.

decisions.choice: Uzzah and Ahio, the sons of Abinadab: his sons or his descendants
decisions.reason: The ark had come to Abinadab's house at least twenty years before Saul's reign (1 Samuel 7:2), so these men may be his grandsons; "sons" can cover later generations. The letters of the name Ahio can also be read "his brother", and the Greek has "his brothers", but the name fits verse 4, where he walks ahead of the ark.

decisions.choice: guiding the cart
decisions.reason: The verb is used of leading or driving animals. Readable says "guiding", since the men walked beside the oxen and steered them.

records.source: וַיִּשָּׂאֻ֗הוּ מִבֵּ֤ית אֲבִֽינָדָב֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בַּגִּבְעָ֔ה עִ֖ם אֲר֣וֹן הָאֱלֹהִ֑ים וְאַחְי֕וֹ הֹלֵ֖ךְ לִפְנֵ֥י הָאָרֽוֹן׃
records.gloss: and they carried it from [the] house of Abinadab which [was] on the hill with [the] ark of the God; and Ahio [was] walking before the ark.
pieces: So they brought the cart out of the house of Abinadab on the hill with the ark of God on it, and Ahio was walking in front of the ark.

L.4: And they carried it from the house of Abinadab, which [was] on the hill, with the ark of God; and Ahio [was] walking before the ark.

R.4: They brought the cart out of Abinadab's house with the ark of God on it. Ahio walked in front of the ark.

decisions.choice: the Hebrew text as it stands, repeating words from verse 3
alternatives: omit the repeated words and read only "with the ark of God, and Ahio was walking before the ark"
decisions.reason: The first words of this verse repeat the end of verse 3 almost word for word. A copyist's eye probably slipped back to the same words, and the Greek has a shorter text; 1 Chronicles 13:7 has neither. Read as it stands, "it" is the new cart, and "with the ark of God" says what it was carrying.

decisions.choice: Ahio walking before the ark: leading the oxen
decisions.reason: Ahio walked ahead to lead the team, while Uzzah stayed by the cart, close enough to reach the ark when the oxen stumbled (verse 6).

decisions.choice: the cart ... with the ark of God on it
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the cart, which "it" refers to, and add "on it" so that "with the ark of God" reads as what the cart carried.

records.source: וְדָוִ֣ד׀וְכָל־בֵּ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל מְשַֽׂחֲקִים֙ לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֔ה בְּכֹ֖ל עֲצֵ֣י בְרוֹשִׁ֑ים וּבְכִנֹּר֤וֹת וּבִנְבָלִים֙ וּבְתֻפִּ֔ים וּבִמְנַֽעַנְעִ֖ים וּֽבְצֶלְצֶלִֽים׃
records.gloss: And David and all [the] house of Israel [were] celebrating before Yahweh with all woods of cypresses, and with lyres and with harps and with tambourines and with rattles and with cymbals.
pieces: David and the whole house of Israel were celebrating before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} with every kind of instrument made of cypress wood, with lyres, harps, tambourines, rattles and cymbals.

L.5: And David and all the house of Israel [were] celebrating before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} with all [kinds of] cypress wood, and with lyres and with harps and with tambourines and with rattles and with cymbals.

R.5: David and all the people of Israel were celebrating in front of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. They played all kinds of instruments made of cypress wood, and lyres, harps, tambourines, rattles and cymbals.

decisions.choice: celebrating: making merry with music and dance
decisions.reason: The verb means "laugh, play, make merry". It is used of women singing and dancing to welcome the victors (1 Samuel 18:7) and of dancing in celebration (Jeremiah 31:4). David uses the same verb when he answers Michal (verse 21).

decisions.choice: before the LORD: in front of the ark, where the LORD was present
decisions.reason: The ark was the place of the LORD's presence (verse 2), so to celebrate before the ark was to celebrate before the LORD himself (also verses 14, 16, 21).

decisions.choice: with all kinds of cypress wood: instruments made of the wood, as the Hebrew text reads
alternatives: with all their might and with songs (1 Chronicles 13:8; the Greek)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew of Samuel reads "with all woods of cypresses", which most naturally means wooden instruments. 1 Chronicles 13:8, telling the same event, reads "with all their might and with songs", and so does the Greek of Samuel. In Hebrew the two readings are written with many of the same letters, so one may have come from the other in copying.

decisions.choice: lyres, harps, tambourines, rattles and cymbals
decisions.reason: The lyre was the small stringed instrument David played (1 Samuel 16:23); the harp was a larger stringed instrument. The tambourine was a hand drum. The word for "rattles" is found only here and comes from a verb meaning "shake"; it was probably a sistrum, a frame with loose rings that jingle. Cymbals were struck metal plates.

decisions.choice: all the people of Israel
decisions.reason: Readable says "the people of Israel" for "the house of Israel", the whole nation.

records.source: וַיָּבֹ֖אוּ עַד־גֹּ֣רֶן נָכ֑וֹן וַיִּשְׁלַ֨ח עֻזָּ֜א אֶל־אֲר֤וֹן הָֽאֱלֹהִים֙ וַיֹּ֣אחֶז בּ֔וֹ כִּ֥י שָׁמְט֖וּ הַבָּקָֽר׃
records.gloss: And they came to [the] threshing floor of Nacon, and sent Uzzah to [the] ark of the God and took hold of it, for stumbled the oxen.
pieces: When they arrived at the threshing floor of Nacon, Uzzah put out his hand and took hold of the ark of God, for the oxen had stumbled.

L.6: And they came to the threshing floor of Nacon, and Uzzah reached out to the ark of God and took hold of it, for the oxen stumbled.

R.6: When they reached the threshing floor of Nacon, the oxen stumbled. Uzzah reached out his hand and grabbed the ark of God to steady it.

decisions.choice: the threshing floor of Nacon: a place on the road, not otherwise known
decisions.reason: A threshing floor was a flat open space of beaten earth or rock where grain was threshed. This one is named only here; 1 Chronicles 13:9 calls it the threshing floor of Chidon. "Nacon" may be a name, or a word meaning "firm" or "prepared".

decisions.choice: reached out: stretched out his hand
decisions.reason: The verb "send" is used without an object, as often when the hand is meant. 1 Chronicles 13:9 says "his hand".

decisions.choice: the oxen stumbled: the cart lurched
decisions.reason: The verb means "let drop" or "let loose". Here it probably means the oxen stumbled or slipped, so that the cart and the ark tipped. Some take it as "the oxen shook it" or "let it slip"; in each case the ark was in danger of falling.

decisions.choice: the oxen stumbled; reached out his hand ... to steady it
decisions.reason: Readable tells the events in the order they happened, putting the oxen's stumble first, adds "his hand" (as m2), and says why Uzzah took hold.

records.source: וַיִּֽחַר־אַ֤ף יְהוָה֙ בְּעֻזָּ֔ה וַיַּכֵּ֥הוּ שָׁ֛ם הָאֱלֹהִ֖ים עַל־הַשַּׁ֑ל וַיָּ֣מָת שָׁ֔ם עִ֖ם אֲר֥וֹן הָאֱלֹהִֽים׃
records.gloss: And burned [the] anger of Yahweh against Uzzah, and struck him there the God for the error, and he died there beside [the] ark of the God.
pieces: Then the anger of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} blazed against Uzzah, and God struck him down there for his error. He died there beside the ark of God.

L.7: And the anger of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} burned against Uzzah, and God struck him there for the error, and he died there beside the ark of God.

R.7: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} was very angry with Uzzah. God struck him down there because of his wrong act, and he died there beside the ark of God.

decisions.choice: for the error: because of his rash fault
alternatives: because he reached out his hand to the ark (1 Chronicles 13:10)
decisions.reason: The noun is found only here. It is usually linked with a word meaning "error" or "negligence" (the same idea is used in Daniel 6:5 and Ezra 4:22), so it names a fault: Uzzah acted rashly with what was holy. Others take it as "irreverence". The Greek does not have the word, and 1 Chronicles 13:10 reads instead "because he put out his hand to the ark", which may be what the short word here means.

decisions.choice: the LORD's anger against Uzzah: the holiness of the ark
decisions.reason: The law warned that even the Levites who carried the holy things must not touch them, or they would die (Numbers 4:15), and many at Beth-shemesh had died for looking into the ark (1 Samuel 6:19). Uzzah meant to protect the ark, but it was holy, and it was being moved in a way the law did not allow (verse 3). The text tells what happened and does not explain further.

decisions.choice: God: the God, the true God
decisions.reason: The verse moves from "the LORD" to "the God", the form used for the ark throughout this story. Both name the same God.

decisions.choice: was very angry
decisions.reason: Readable says "was very angry" for the picture of anger that "burned".

records.source: וַיִּ֣חַר לְדָוִ֔ד עַל֩ אֲשֶׁ֨ר פָּרַ֧ץ יְהוָ֛ה פֶּ֖רֶץ בְּעֻזָּ֑ה וַיִּקְרָ֞א לַמָּק֤וֹם הַהוּא֙ פֶּ֣רֶץ עֻזָּ֔ה עַ֖ד הַיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה׃
records.gloss: And it burned to David because broke out Yahweh [a] breaking out against Uzzah; and he called the place that Perez-uzzah until the day the this.
pieces: David was angry because {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had burst out against Uzzah, and he named that place Perez-uzzah, a name it still has to this day.

L.8: And David was angry because {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had broken out [with] a breaking out against Uzzah; and he called that place Perez-uzzah, to this day.

R.8: David was angry because {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had burst out against Uzzah. So he named that place Perez-uzzah, which means "bursting out against Uzzah". It still has that name to this day.

decisions.choice: David was angry
decisions.reason: The verb is the same "burn" used of the LORD's anger in verse 7, here without the word "anger". It may also mean that David was deeply upset or distressed, as with Jonah (Jonah 4:1, 4). The text does not say whether his anger was against the LORD, against himself, or at what had happened.

decisions.choice: broken out ... Perez-uzzah: the LORD's outburst against Uzzah
decisions.reason: The verb "break out, burst through" and the noun from it give the place its name, Perez-uzzah, "breaking out against Uzzah". In the chapter before, David named Baal-perazim because the LORD had "broken out" against his enemies like a flood (5:20). Now the LORD breaks out against one of his own people. The same word is used of the LORD's warning at Sinai not to come too near, "or he will break out against them" (Exodus 19:22, 24).

decisions.choice: to this day: the writer's own day
decisions.reason: As in 4:3: the name was still in use when the account was written.

decisions.choice: which means "bursting out against Uzzah"
decisions.reason: Readable explains the meaning of the name, which the Hebrew reader would hear at once.

records.source: וַיִּרָ֥א דָוִ֛ד אֶת־יְהוָ֖ה בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֑וּא וַיֹּ֕אמֶר אֵ֛יךְ יָב֥וֹא אֵלַ֖י אֲר֥וֹן יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: And feared David Yahweh on the day the that, and he said, How will come to me [the] ark of Yahweh?
pieces: David was afraid of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} that day, and he said, "How can the ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} ever come to me?"

L.9: And David feared {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} on that day, and he said, "How shall the ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} come to me?"

R.9: That day David was afraid of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. He said, "How can the ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} ever come to stay with me?"

decisions.choice: feared the LORD: was afraid of him
decisions.reason: The verb can mean reverence or awe, but here, after Uzzah's death, it is plain fear of what the LORD might do.

decisions.choice: How can the ark come to me?: a question of fear and doubt
decisions.reason: The question does not ask for a method. It means that David no longer dares to bring the ark into his own city (verse 10). "To me" means to the place where David lives and rules.

decisions.choice: come to stay with me
decisions.reason: Readable adds "to stay", since David was bringing the ark to his city to remain there.

records.source: וְלֹֽא־אָבָ֣ה דָוִ֗ד לְהָסִ֥יר אֵלָ֛יו אֶת־אֲר֥וֹן יְהוָ֖ה עַל־עִ֣יר דָּוִ֑ד וַיַּטֵּ֣הוּ דָוִ֔ד בֵּ֥ית עֹבֵֽד־אֱד֖וֹם הַגִּתִּֽי׃
records.gloss: And not was willing David to turn aside to him [the] ark of Yahweh to [the] city of David; and turned it aside David [to the] house of Obed-Edom the Gittite.
pieces: So David was not willing to take the ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} into the city of David to be with him. Instead he turned aside and took it to the house of Obed-Edom the Gittite.

L.10: And David was not willing to move the ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} to himself, into the city of David; and David turned it aside [to the] house of Obed-Edom the Gittite.

R.10: So David decided not to take the ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} home with him to the city of David. Instead, he had it taken off the road to the house of a man named Obed-Edom, who came from Gath.

decisions.choice: the city of David: the stronghold of Zion
decisions.reason: David had captured the Jebusite stronghold of Zion and named it the city of David (5:7, 9). It was the oldest part of Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: Obed-Edom the Gittite: a man from a town called Gath
decisions.reason: "Gittite" means a man from Gath. This could be the Philistine city, since David had men from there among his followers (15:18-19). It could also be Gath-rimmon, a town given to the Levites (Joshua 21:24-25), and 1 Chronicles 15:18, 24 and 16:38 name an Obed-Edom among the Levite gatekeepers and musicians who served the ark. The text here does not say which.

decisions.choice: had it taken off the road; who came from Gath
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what "turned it aside" means and what "Gittite" means.

records.source: וַיֵּשֶׁב֩ אֲר֨וֹן יְהוָ֜ה בֵּ֣ית עֹבֵ֥ד אֱדֹ֛ם הַגִּתִּ֖י שְׁלֹשָׁ֣ה חֳדָשִׁ֑ים וַיְבָ֧רֶךְ יְהוָ֛ה אֶת־עֹבֵ֥ד אֱדֹ֖ם וְאֶת־כָּל־בֵּיתֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And remained [the] ark of Yahweh [at the] house of Obed-Edom the Gittite three months; and blessed Yahweh Obed-Edom and all his household.
pieces: The ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} stayed three months at the house of Obed-Edom the Gittite, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} blessed Obed-Edom and his whole household.

L.11: And the ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} remained [at the] house of Obed-Edom the Gittite three months, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} blessed Obed-Edom and all his household.

R.11: The ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} stayed at Obed-Edom's house for three months. And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} blessed Obed-Edom and his whole household.

decisions.choice: the LORD blessed Obed-Edom: the ark brings blessing as well as judgment
decisions.reason: The same ark that had brought death to Uzzah brought good to the household that kept it. The ark had also brought disaster on the Philistines who held it (1 Samuel 5). 1 Chronicles 26:4-5 speaks of the many sons God gave Obed-Edom.

decisions.choice: household: his family and everyone who lived under his care
decisions.reason: The word "house" here means the household: family, servants and goods (compare verse 12, "all that is his").

records.source: וַיֻּגַּ֗ד לַמֶּ֣לֶךְ דָּוִד֮ לֵאמֹר֒ בֵּרַ֣ךְ יְהוָ֗ה אֶת־בֵּ֨ית עֹבֵ֤ד אֱדֹם֙ וְאֶת־כָּל־אֲשֶׁר־ל֔וֹ בַּעֲב֖וּר אֲר֣וֹן הָאֱלֹהִ֑ים וַיֵּ֣לֶךְ דָּוִ֗ד וַיַּעַל֩ אֶת־אֲר֨וֹן הָאֱלֹהִ֜ים מִבֵּ֨ית עֹבֵ֥ד אֱדֹ֛ם עִ֥יר דָּוִ֖ד בְּשִׂמְחָֽה׃
records.gloss: And it was told to the king David, saying, Has blessed Yahweh [the] house of Obed-Edom and all that [is] to him because of [the] ark of the God. And went David and brought up [the] ark of the God from [the] house of Obed-Edom [to the] city of David with joy.
pieces: King David was told, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has blessed the household of Obed-Edom and everything he has because of the ark of God." So David went and brought the ark of God up from the house of Obed-Edom to the city of David with rejoicing.

L.12: And it was told to King David, saying, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has blessed the house of Obed-Edom and all that [is] his, because of the ark of God." And David went and brought up the ark of God from the house of Obed-Edom [to the] city of David with rejoicing.

R.12: Someone told King David, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has blessed Obed-Edom's family and everything he owns, because the ark of God is there." So David went with great joy and brought the ark of God up from Obed-Edom's house to the city of David.

decisions.choice: blessed because of the ark: the LORD's presence brings good where he is honored
decisions.reason: The report answers David's fear (verse 9). The ark had not only brought death; where it was kept with care, the LORD blessed. This gives David the courage to try again.

decisions.choice: with rejoicing: with celebration
decisions.reason: The word means joy shown openly, with feasting, music and dancing, as the next verses describe (verses 13-15).

decisions.choice: brought up: carried up to the higher city
decisions.reason: Jerusalem stood high in the hill country, so going there is "going up"; the same verb is used for bringing the ark from Baale-judah (verse 2).

decisions.choice: Someone told; because the ark of God is there
decisions.reason: Readable gives the passive "it was told" a subject and says what "because of the ark" means.

records.source: וַיְהִ֗י כִּ֧י צָעֲד֛וּ נֹשְׂאֵ֥י אֲרוֹן־יְהוָ֖ה שִׁשָּׁ֣ה צְעָדִ֑ים וַיִּזְבַּ֥ח שׁ֖וֹר וּמְרִֽיא׃
records.gloss: And it was, when had stepped [the] carriers of [the] ark of Yahweh six steps, and he sacrificed an ox and a fatling.
pieces: When those carrying the ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had gone six steps, David sacrificed an ox and a fattened calf.

L.13: And it happened, when those carrying the ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had gone six steps, [that] he sacrificed an ox and a fatling.

R.13: This time men carried the ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. When they had gone six steps, David offered an ox and a fattened calf as a sacrifice.

decisions.choice: those carrying the ark: carried this time, not set on a cart
decisions.reason: On the first attempt the ark rode on a cart (verse 3). Now it is carried, as the law required (Numbers 4:15; 7:9); 1 Chronicles 15:2, 13-15 says the Levites carried it on poles on their shoulders.

decisions.choice: after six steps, he sacrificed: once, at the start of the journey
decisions.reason: The sentence most naturally means that after the first six steps, when the carriers had come to no harm, David stopped and offered a sacrifice. Some have read it as a sacrifice every six steps, but the Hebrew does not say "every". 1 Chronicles 15:26 adds that seven bulls and seven rams were sacrificed because God helped the Levites who carried the ark.

decisions.choice: an ox and a fatling: a bull and a fattened animal
decisions.reason: The second word means an animal fattened for sacrifice or a feast, usually a young bull or calf (Isaiah 11:6).

decisions.choice: David sacrificed; This time men carried
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name David as the one who sacrificed. Readable adds "This time" to show the change from the cart in verse 3.

records.source: וְדָוִ֛ד מְכַרְכֵּ֥ר בְּכָל־עֹ֖ז לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה וְדָוִ֕ד חָג֖וּר אֵפ֥וֹד בָּֽד׃
records.gloss: And David [was] whirling with all strength before Yahweh; and David [was] girded [with an] ephod of linen.
pieces: David was dancing before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} with all his might, and he was wearing a linen ephod.

L.14: And David [was] whirling with all [his] strength before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and David [was] girded [with] a linen ephod.

R.14: David danced with all his strength in front of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. He was wearing a linen ephod, a simple garment like the ones priests wore.

decisions.choice: whirling: dancing, spinning round
decisions.reason: The verb is found only here and in verse 16. It seems to describe a turning, whirling dance done with full energy.

decisions.choice: a linen ephod: the plain garment of those who served at the sanctuary
decisions.reason: The boy Samuel wore a linen ephod while serving the LORD at Shiloh (1 Samuel 2:18), and the priests of Nob were "men who wore the linen ephod" (1 Samuel 22:18). It was a short garment tied around the body, not the high priest's ephod of gold and colored yarn (Exodus 28:6-14). David leads the worship in clothes of service rather than in royal robes, and the short garment explains Michal's words in verse 20.

decisions.choice: dancing
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "dancing"; Literal keeps the picture of "whirling".

decisions.choice: a simple garment like the ones priests wore
decisions.reason: Readable explains the ephod, a word most readers will not know.

records.source: וְדָוִד֙ וְכָל־בֵּ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל מַעֲלִ֖ים אֶת־אֲר֣וֹן יְהוָ֑ה בִּתְרוּעָ֖ה וּבְק֥וֹל שׁוֹפָֽר׃
records.gloss: And David and all [the] house of Israel [were] bringing up [the] ark of Yahweh with shouting and with [the] sound of [the] ram's horn.
pieces: So David and the whole house of Israel brought up the ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} with loud shouts of joy and the sound of the ram's horn.

L.15: And David and all the house of Israel [were] bringing up the ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} with shouting and with the sound of the ram's horn.

R.15: So David and all the people of Israel brought the ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} up to the city. They shouted with joy, and the ram's horn was blown.

decisions.choice: shouting: a loud shout of acclaim
decisions.reason: The word is used for a battle cry and for the joyful shout that greets a king or the LORD. When the ark came into Israel's camp before the battle with the Philistines, Israel raised the same great shout (1 Samuel 4:5); here it is the shout of a procession welcoming the LORD as king.

decisions.choice: the ram's horn: the shofar
decisions.reason: The ram's horn was blown for signals in war and for festivals and holy days (Leviticus 25:9; Joshua 6:4-5).

decisions.choice: shouts of joy
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable add "of joy", since the setting makes clear it is a shout of celebration, not of battle.

decisions.choice: all the people of Israel
decisions.reason: As in verse 5.

records.source: וְהָיָה֙ אֲר֣וֹן יְהוָ֔ה בָּ֖א עִ֣יר דָּוִ֑ד וּמִיכַ֨ל בַּת־שָׁא֜וּל נִשְׁקְפָ֣ה׀בְּעַ֣ד הַחַלּ֗וֹן וַתֵּ֨רֶא אֶת־הַמֶּ֤לֶךְ דָּוִד֙ מְפַזֵּ֤ז וּמְכַרְכֵּר֙ לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֔ה וַתִּ֥בֶז ל֖וֹ בְּלִבָּֽהּ׃
records.gloss: And it was, [the] ark of Yahweh [was] coming [into the] city of David, and Michal [the] daughter of Saul looked down through the window and saw the king David leaping and whirling before Yahweh, and she despised him in her heart.
pieces: As the ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was coming into the city of David, Michal the daughter of Saul looked down from the window. She saw King David leaping and dancing before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and in her heart she despised him.

L.16: And it happened, [as] the ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came [into the] city of David, Michal the daughter of Saul looked down through the window and saw King David leaping and whirling before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and she despised him in her heart.

R.16: As the ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was coming into the city of David, Saul's daughter Michal looked out of a window. She saw King David jumping and dancing in front of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and in her heart she despised him.

decisions.choice: Michal the daughter of Saul: named by her father, not as David's wife
decisions.reason: Michal was David's first wife (1 Samuel 18:27), taken from him by Saul and given back to him (3:13-16). Here and in verses 20 and 23 the writer calls her "the daughter of Saul", which points to the house of Saul that the LORD had set aside for David (verse 21).

decisions.choice: despised him: looked on him with contempt
decisions.reason: The verb means to count someone as worthless. It is used of the men who despised Saul at his choosing (1 Samuel 10:27) and of Goliath despising David (1 Samuel 17:42).

decisions.choice: leaping and whirling
decisions.reason: The first verb means to leap or spring; the second is the whirling dance of verse 14.

decisions.choice: dancing
decisions.reason: As in verse 14.

records.source: וַיָּבִ֜אוּ אֶת־אֲר֣וֹן יְהוָ֗ה וַיַּצִּ֤גוּ אֹתוֹ֙ בִּמְקוֹמ֔וֹ בְּת֣וֹךְ הָאֹ֔הֶל אֲשֶׁ֥ר נָטָה־ל֖וֹ דָּוִ֑ד וַיַּ֨עַל דָּוִ֥ד עֹל֛וֹת לִפְנֵ֥י יְהוָ֖ה וּשְׁלָמִֽים׃
records.gloss: And they brought [the] ark of Yahweh and set it in its place in [the] midst of the tent that pitched for it David; and offered up David burnt offerings before Yahweh and peace offerings.
pieces: They carried the ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} in and set it in its place within the tent David had pitched for it. David then offered burnt offerings and peace offerings before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.17: And they brought in the ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and set it in its place inside the tent that David had pitched for it; and David offered burnt offerings before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and peace offerings.

R.17: They brought the ark of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} into the tent David had set up for it, and put it in its place there. Then David offered burnt offerings and peace offerings to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: the tent David had pitched: a new tent in Jerusalem
decisions.reason: This was a tent David set up for the ark in his city, not the old tent of meeting, which 1 Chronicles 16:39 and 21:29 place at Gibeon. The ark stays in a tent until the temple is built (7:2, 6).

decisions.choice: burnt offerings and peace offerings
decisions.reason: A burnt offering was burned whole on the altar as a gift to God (Leviticus 1). Most of a peace offering was eaten by the worshipers in a shared meal (Leviticus 3; 7:11-15), which explains the food given out in verse 19.

decisions.choice: David offered: the king brought the offerings
decisions.reason: The king is named as the one who offered, as Solomon is later (1 Kings 8:62-64). The text does not say whether priests did the work at the altar for him.

decisions.choice: offered burnt offerings and peace offerings before the LORD
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable put the two kinds of offering together; Readable says "to the LORD" for "before the LORD".

records.source: וַיְכַ֣ל דָּוִ֔ד מֵהַעֲל֥וֹת הָעוֹלָ֖ה וְהַשְּׁלָמִ֑ים וַיְבָ֣רֶךְ אֶת־הָעָ֔ם בְּשֵׁ֖ם יְהוָ֥ה צְבָאֽוֹת׃
records.gloss: And finished David from offering up the burnt offering and the peace offerings, and he blessed the people in [the] name of Yahweh of hosts.
pieces: When David had finished offering the burnt offerings and the peace offerings, he pronounced a blessing on the people in the name of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies.

L.18: And David finished offering the burnt offering and the peace offerings, and he blessed the people in the name of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts.

R.18: When David was done with the burnt offerings and peace offerings, he spoke a blessing over the people in the name of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies.

decisions.choice: the burnt offering: all the burnt offerings
decisions.reason: The singular stands for the whole group of burnt offerings named in verse 17.

decisions.choice: blessed the people in the name of the LORD of hosts
decisions.reason: To bless in the LORD's name is to call down his good on people, speaking for him (Numbers 6:23-27). David does this as king leading the worship, as Solomon does when the temple is dedicated (1 Kings 8:14, 55). The full title of verse 2 returns at the close of the procession.

decisions.choice: the LORD of Armies
decisions.reason: As in verse 2.

records.source: וַיְחַלֵּ֨ק לְכָל־הָעָ֜ם לְכָל־הֲמ֣וֹן יִשְׂרָאֵל֮ לְמֵאִ֣ישׁ וְעַד־אִשָּׁה֒ לְאִ֗ישׁ חַלַּ֥ת לֶ֨חֶם֙ אַחַ֔ת וְאֶשְׁפָּ֣ר אֶחָ֔ד וַאֲשִׁישָׁ֖ה אֶחָ֑ת וַיֵּ֥לֶךְ כָּל־הָעָ֖ם אִ֥ישׁ לְבֵיתֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And he distributed to all the people, to all [the] multitude of Israel, from man and to woman, to each cake of bread one and date-cake one and raisin-cake one; and went all the people, each to his house.
pieces: He also handed out food to all the people, the whole crowd of Israel, both men and women: a loaf of bread, a cake of dates and a cake of raisins for each one. Then all the people went home, each to {{gender:their|his}} own house.

L.19: And he distributed to all the people, to all the crowd of Israel, from man to woman, to each one cake of bread and one date cake and one raisin cake. And all the people went, each to {{gender:their|his}} house.

R.19: He gave food to every person in the crowd of Israel, both men and women. Each one received a loaf of bread, a cake of dates and a cake of raisins. Then everyone went home.

decisions.choice: to the whole crowd, men and women: a feast for all
decisions.reason: Women as well as men were given a share. The meal belonged with the peace offerings (verse 17), a feast of joy before the LORD.

decisions.choice: a cake of bread; a raisin cake
decisions.reason: The first is a round loaf, sometimes ring-shaped. The raisin cake was made of pressed dried grapes and was festival food (Hosea 3:1; Song of Songs 2:5).

decisions.choice: a date cake: meaning uncertain
decisions.reason: The word is found only here and in the same account at 1 Chronicles 16:3, and its meaning is not known for certain. It may be a cake of dates, or a portion of meat from the sacrifices; older guesses include a measure of wine.

decisions.choice: a loaf of bread
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "loaf" for "cake of bread", the ordinary English word for a single bread.

decisions.choice: each to their house
decisions.reason: The people are men and women, so the inclusive form is the default and "his" the alternative. Readable says "everyone", which needs no setting.

records.source: וַיָּ֥שָׁב דָּוִ֖ד לְבָרֵ֣ךְ אֶת־בֵּית֑וֹ וַתֵּצֵ֞א מִיכַ֤ל בַּת־שָׁאוּל֙ לִקְרַ֣את דָּוִ֔ד וַתֹּ֗אמֶר מַה־נִּכְבַּ֨ד הַיּ֜וֹם מֶ֣לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל אֲשֶׁ֨ר נִגְלָ֤ה הַיּוֹם֙ לְעֵינֵ֨י אַמְה֣וֹת עֲבָדָ֔יו כְּהִגָּל֥וֹת נִגְל֖וֹת אַחַ֥ד הָרֵקִֽים׃
records.gloss: And returned David to bless his household; and came out Michal [the] daughter of Saul to meet David and said, How honored himself today [the] king of Israel, who uncovered himself today in [the] eyes of [the] maidservants of his servants, as uncovers himself shamelessly one of the worthless [men]!
pieces: When David returned home to bless his household, Saul's daughter Michal came out to meet him. She said, "How the king of Israel has honored himself today! He has uncovered himself today before the eyes of his officials' servant girls, as shamelessly as some worthless fellow would!"

L.20: And David returned to bless his household, and Michal the daughter of Saul came out to meet David and said, "How the king of Israel honored himself today, who uncovered himself today in the eyes of the slave girls of his servants, as one of the worthless [men] shamelessly uncovers himself!"

R.20: When David went home to bless his family, Michal, Saul's daughter, came out to meet him. She said, "What honor the king of Israel won for himself today! He uncovered his body in front of the servant girls of his officials, as shamelessly as any worthless fellow!"

decisions.choice: How the king of Israel honored himself today!: bitter mockery
decisions.reason: Michal says the opposite of what she means: in her eyes the king has disgraced himself. The word "honor" is taken up again by David in verse 22, where he says he will be honored by the very women she speaks of.

decisions.choice: uncovered himself: exposed his body
decisions.reason: The verb means "uncover, lay bare", and the repeated form stresses it. Dancing hard in a short linen ephod (verse 14), David showed more of his body than she thought fitting for a king. The text does not say he was naked.

decisions.choice: one of the worthless men: a low, good-for-nothing fellow
decisions.reason: The word means "empty" and is used of reckless, worthless men (Judges 9:4; 11:3).

decisions.choice: the slave girls of his servants: the lowest women in the city
decisions.reason: These are female slaves belonging to the king's officials. Michal, a king's daughter, sets them against the dignity of the king.

decisions.choice: servant girls; officials
decisions.reason: As elsewhere, Literal says "slave" and Balanced and Readable "servant" for these women; the king's "servants" are his officials, as in these books.

decisions.choice: uncovered his body
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what "uncovered himself" means, without going beyond it.

records.source: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר דָּוִד֮ אֶל־מִיכַל֒ לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֗ה אֲשֶׁ֨ר בָּֽחַר־בִּ֤י מֵֽאָבִיךְ֙ וּמִכָּל־בֵּית֔וֹ לְצַוֺּ֨ת אֹתִ֥י נָגִ֛יד עַל־עַ֥ם יְהוָ֖ה עַל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וְשִׂחַקְתִּ֖י לִפְנֵ֥י יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: And said David to Michal, Before Yahweh, who chose me over your father and over all his house to appoint me ruler over [the] people of Yahweh, over Israel, and I will celebrate before Yahweh.
pieces: David said to Michal, "It was before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} that I danced, before the one who chose me over your father and over all his family and appointed me ruler over Israel, the people of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. I will celebrate before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.21: And David said to Michal, "Before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, who chose me over your father and over all his house to appoint me ruler over the people of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, over Israel, I will celebrate before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.21: David answered Michal, "I was dancing for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. He chose me instead of your father or anyone in his family. He made me the leader of Israel, the people of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. So I will celebrate in front of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: Before the LORD ...: it was before the LORD that I did it
alternatives: Before the LORD I danced; blessed be the LORD, who chose me (the Greek)
decisions.reason: David begins "Before the LORD" and does not finish the thought, then ends with "I will celebrate before the LORD". The sense is: what I did, I did before the LORD. The Greek fills it out: "Before the LORD I danced; blessed be the LORD, who chose me ...". The Hebrew is followed here.

decisions.choice: who chose me over your father and all his house
decisions.reason: David reminds Saul's daughter that the LORD rejected Saul and chose David in his place (1 Samuel 13:13-14; 15:28; 16:1). His dancing was worship of the God who made him king, not a show for others.

decisions.choice: ruler: the one the LORD appoints to lead his people
decisions.reason: The word was used when the LORD chose a man after his own heart to lead his people (1 Samuel 13:14; 25:30).

decisions.choice: celebrate
decisions.reason: The same verb as in verse 5: to make merry, with music and dance.

decisions.choice: It was before the LORD that I danced; I was dancing for the LORD
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable supply "I danced" so that David's unfinished opening reads as a sentence (see m1).

decisions.choice: leader
decisions.reason: Readable says "leader" for the word Literal and Balanced render "ruler", as in these books.

records.source: וּנְקַלֹּ֤תִי עוֹד֙ מִזֹּ֔את וְהָיִ֥יתִי שָׁפָ֖ל בְּעֵינָ֑י וְעִם־הָֽאֲמָהוֹת֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר אָמַ֔רְתְּ עִמָּ֖ם אִכָּבֵֽדָה׃
records.gloss: And I will be lightly esteemed still more than this, and I will be low in my eyes; and with the maidservants of whom you have spoken, with them I will be honored.
pieces: I will make myself even more undignified than this, and I will be humble in my own eyes. But by the servant girls you spoke of, by them I will be held in honor."

L.22: And I will be more lightly esteemed still than this, and I will be low in my [own] eyes; but with the slave girls of whom you have spoken, with them I will be honored."

R.22: I am willing to look even more foolish than this and to be humble in my own eyes. But those servant girls you talked about will honor me."

decisions.choice: lightly esteemed ... honored: "light" set against "heavy"
decisions.reason: The verb for "be lightly esteemed" comes from a word for "light, of little weight"; the word for "honor" comes from a word for "heavy, weighty". David answers Michal's mocking "honored" (verse 20): he is ready to be thought of little weight, and it is among the lowly that he will have honor.

decisions.choice: in my own eyes: as the Hebrew text reads
decisions.reason: The Greek reads "in your eyes", which would mean "I will be low in your sight". The Hebrew has David say he will be humble in his own sight.

decisions.choice: low ... honored: the LORD lifts the lowly
decisions.reason: The words echo Hannah's song: the LORD brings low and lifts up, and gives the poor a seat of honor (1 Samuel 2:7-8).

decisions.choice: servant girls
decisions.reason: As in verse 20.

records.gloss: And to Michal [the] daughter of Saul there was not to her [a] child until [the] day of her death.
pieces: And Michal the daughter of Saul had no child until the day she died.

L.23: And Michal the daughter of Saul had no child to the day of her death.

R.23: Michal, Saul's daughter, never had any children as long as she lived.

decisions.choice: Michal had no child: Saul's line would not continue through David's house
decisions.reason: The writer does not say whether this was the LORD's judgment or because David no longer lived with her as a husband. Either way, no child of Saul's daughter would sit on David's throne. (In 21:8 the Hebrew names "Michal" as the mother of five sons, but that is probably an error for her sister Merab, as 1 Samuel 18:19 shows.)
